samples.summary: New `MaxMergeEntries` cap does not bound the *product* of entries × cells-per-merge — a ~260 KB `PUT merges` still builds a 1e9-entry merge cover map and permanently bricks the tab
samples.evidence: `parseMerges` now enforces two independent ceilings: `entries.length <= 10_000` (worksheet-settings.ts:141) and `rs * cs <= 100_000` per span (worksheet-settings.ts:174). Nothing bounds their product. `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap()` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:851-863) loops `for (r) for (c) { toSref(); mergeCoverMap.set(...) }` over *every* entry, so the load-time cost is the sum of `rs*cs` across entries, not the max. Attack: PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/tabs/:t/merges with 10,000 anchors in distinct columns — `{"A1":{"rs":100000,"cs":1},"B1":{"rs":100000,"cs":1}, ...}` — each entry ~26 bytes, ~260 KB total, far under the 25 MB `JSON_BODY_LIMIT` (packages/backend/src/main.ts:20) and accepted by every check in `parseMerges` (each span is exactly at the 100,000 ceiling, each anchor round-trips through `toSref(parseRef(ref))`, each stays inside the grid). On the next document load every collaborator's `Sheet.loadMerges()` -> `rebuildMergeCoverMap()` performs 1e9 `toSref` calls and 1e9 `Map.set` inserts with distinct string keys: the tab hangs and then OOMs the renderer, for every user, on every load. That is exactly the 'a document nobody can open again' outcome the `MaxMergedCells` comment (worksheet-settings.ts:13-23) says the cap exists to prevent; the new entry cap raises the reachable worst case from 1e5 to 1e10 cover-map operations rather than bounding it. No client-side guard exists: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1010-1018 copies the whole map into the Sheet unchecked. Recovery requires another API call, which a hung browser cannot make. Fix: cap the summed `rs*cs` across the map (e.g. a single `MaxTotalMergedCells`), not just each span and the entry count separately.

samples.summary: `MaxMergeEntries` is enforced only on the REST path; the Yorkie CRDT sync path writes `ws.merges` with no cap, so the new gate is bypassable by any client with document edit access
samples.evidence: The cap added at worksheet-settings.ts:141 only runs for `PUT .../merges` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet.controller.ts:234). The other writer of the same field is the collaborative client: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:961-982 (`setMerge`) does `root.sheets[tabId].merges[sref] = {...span}` inside `doc.update` with no count or span validation, and the backend never inspects document content on sync (no server-side validation of `merges` exists — grep for `.merges` under packages/backend/src finds only the settings/structure controllers, which read it). A modified or scripted client holding ordinary document edit rights can therefore push an arbitrary number of merge entries (and arbitrarily large spans) straight into the CRDT, reaching exactly the state the new ceiling is meant to make unreachable, while the presence of the ceiling makes the surface read as covered. This is a property of the CRDT path rather than of the line the delta added, but it is the bypass for the gate the delta introduces, so it belongs with it: the cap should be documented as best-effort for the REST surface only, or backed by a check on the document-load/apply path.

samples.summary: `parseMerges` accepts overlapping merge spans, a state the editor's own merge path never produces
samples.evidence: The validator checks each entry in isolation (round-tripping key, grid bound, per-span cell ceiling) but never checks entries against each other, so `{"A1":{"rs":10,"cs":10},"A5":{"rs":10,"cs":10}}` is stored verbatim (worksheet-settings.ts:146-182). `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:851-863) then maps a covered cell to whichever anchor happened to be iterated last, and `A5` ends up both a merge anchor and a covered cell of `A1` — a state `canMergeSelection`/`mergeSelection` cannot create in the editor. Impact appears limited to rendering/selection confusion rather than a crash (I could not trace an unbounded loop or throw), hence low confidence; noted here as an input-validation gap on an attacker-controlled map that the surrounding comments treat as fully validated.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location verifies. `MaxMergeEntries = 10000` is declared at packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:43 and enforced only inside `parseMerges` at worksheet-settings.ts:141-145; `parseMerges` has exactly one production caller, `@Put('merges')` at packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet.controller.ts:226-234. The same `merges` field is written by the collaborative client at packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:969 and :980 with no entry-count or span validation, and nothing on the backend inspects CRDT content on sync — the only backend references to `.merges` are readers (worksheet.controller.ts:113, :217; worksheet-structure/dimensions/styles controllers; lakehouse.service.ts), and packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:1-31 documents the Yorkie webhook as a read/write *verb* gate only, with no change-pack content inspection. So the ceiling is bypassable by any client with document edit rights. The repo's own rationale at worksheet-settings.ts:30-36 states the threat as an unbounded synchronous walk inside `doc.update` that "blocks the whole Node process ... on every later request that touches the tab", and that walk is reachable from the backend (snapFreezePastMerges at worksheet.controller.ts:112-116), giving the unbounded state a cross-tenant availability blast radius rather than being self-harm only. I weighed refuting as out-of-scope (no privilege boundary is crossed: the CRDT writer needs write permission just as the REST caller does), but the mitigation is genuinely incomplete on a surface the code treats as security-relevant, so the high bar for refutation is not met.

mergedFrom.summary: `parseMerges` caps the cells per merge but not the number of merge entries, leaving the merge map an unbounded attacker-controlled input to every merge-walking code path (now including insert/delete)

finding.summary: `parseMerges` bounds each individual span but places no cap on the *number* of merge entries, which is what makes the new repeated-scan freeze snap (and the pre-existing per-load `rebuildMergeCoverMap` walk) attacker-amplifiable.
finding.evidence: `parseMerges` validates key round-trip, grid bounds and `rs*cs <= MaxMergedCells` per entry, but the loop at worksheet-settings.ts:121 accepts an unbounded entry count; with the 25MB body limit (main.ts:20) that is ~1M merges. Every consumer added by this change iterates that map — `snapFreezePastMerges` repeatedly (merging.ts:217), `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` once per move (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:192) — and `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:851) walks `rs*cs` per entry on every document load, so the same body also makes the tab expensive-to-open for every collaborator. A `MaxMerges` count cap alongside `MaxMergedCells` would remove the amplifier the new snap depends on.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `parseMerges` places no cap on the number of merge entries. It does. `packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:43` declares `const MaxMergeEntries = 10000;` and lines 140-145 enforce it — `const entries = Object.entries(merges); if (entries.length > MaxMergeEntries) throw new BadRequestException(...)` — BEFORE the per-entry loop, which actually starts at line 147 (the finding cites line 121, which is inside a doc comment, indicating stale line numbers). The constant's doc comment (lines 25-42) names precisely the threat the finding describes: rebuildMergeCoverMap on load, snapFreezePastMerges repeatedly on freeze, assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze per move, and the 25MB body limit as the otherwise-only bound (~1M entries). The cap is on the enforced request path: the sole PUT merges handler calls parseMerges(body) at worksheet.controller.ts:234 before doc.update. A regression test at worksheet-settings.spec.ts:114-124 asserts 10001 entries throws and 10000 is accepted. The reviewer's greps missed it on naming: the constant is MaxMergeEntries (not MaxMerges/MAX_MERGES), the code uses Object.entries (not Object.keys(merges)), and the message reads "above the 10000 limit" (not "too many"). The finding's stated remedy is already implemented, adjacent to the MaxMergedCells check it says it should sit alongside.
